persons.name: Bora Özkent
persons.digest:
According to Bora Özkent, yesterday's Nasdaq drop is not a collapse but a rotation out of AI into safer areas: the equal-weighted S&P 500 closed positive while the Nasdaq 100 fell 3%. Financing is at the center; **Meta** was sold hard because free cash flow turned negative and it plans to spend hundreds of billions, and **Lam Research** and **Western Digital** also fell despite good earnings. Technically the Nasdaq Composite could slide about 1,000 points toward its 200-day average (25,000); **OpenAI**'s $30 billion round is a relieving piece of news.

Safe-haven demand for Treasuries pushed yields lower while **Iran** tensions push oil up. Bora Özkent is nearly 100% in stocks in his own portfolio, wants to stay long-term but will sell some losing stocks for tax benefits; he says the elections and November tax-loss selling will bring volatility.

items.title: Stocks Are Solid But Nasdaq Is Collapsing !
items.summary: According to Bora Özkent, yesterday the Dow closed flat while the S&P 500 fell 1.2% and the Nasdaq 100 fell 3%; since the equal-weighted S&P 500 was positive, this is not a collapse but a rotation out of AI into safer areas. Financing is at the center: Meta's earnings were very good but free cash flow turned negative and plans to spend hundreds of billions of dollars scared the market; Meta also plans a two-for-one split creating new shares without voting rights. Micron's earnings are solid, but if Meta and Neo Clouds like CoreWeave cannot raise money, investment stops and Nvidia and Micron would be hit too, he says. Lam Research gave a lower-than-expected growth target because of supply constraints, and Western Digital reported great earnings but was sold on competition worries. The Nasdaq Composite is below its 50-day average; the 200-day average is at 25,000 while the index is at 26,000, so there is a risk of about 1,000 more points down. Safe-haven demand for Treasuries pushed yields lower, and Iran tensions are pushing oil up. OpenAI cutting its valuation target from $1.4 trillion to $1.25 trillion and being close to raising $30 billion is a positive signal for the Anthropic IPO. Bora Özkent is nearly 100% in stocks in his own portfolio, wants to stay long-term but took a serious loss; he will sell some losing stocks for tax benefits and says the elections and November tax-loss selling will bring volatility.

assets.note: Free cash flow turned negative and the plan to spend hundreds of billions scared the market.
Nasdaq 100 fell 3% yesterday; the Composite's 200-day average is at 25,000 and the index is at 26,000.
Earnings and cash flow are very strong, but it would be hit if Meta and Neo Clouds cannot raise money.
